Subject: Orion Health discovery follow-up — recommended evals and quant tradeoffs

Hi Asha / Liam,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to understand the three primary objectives you called out:
- real-time triage (sub-200ms p50 on short prompts),
- long-form summarization of clinical notes (multi-paragraph, high-fidelity), and
- tight cost targets for a pilot at ~1M tokens/month.

Based on the samples you shared and the latency targets, here's our recommended starting plan for a 6-week PoC:

1) Candidate models to evaluate (short-list):
   - Llama-3-13B (standard FP16) — strong baseline for instruction-following and summarization.
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP16) — good token-efficiency for short-answer triage tasks.
   - rwinf-13B-opt (Redwood-verified, quant-friendly) — our optimized candidate for throughput once quantized.

2) Compression/quantization variants to test:
   - AWQ (8-bit asymmetric) — low-quality delta in our other healthcare POCs while getting 2.5x throughput improvement; low deployment risk because we can fall back.
   - GPTQ (int4/int8 variants) — better peak compression on some architectures, but sometimes brittle on long-form outputs.
   - FP8 (hardware FP8 where available) — best throughput but highest risk for subtle summary regressions on long clinical text.

3) Evaluation plan (baseline + regression gating):
   - Baseline: run 1k representative prompts (attached eval_prompt_set_v2.txt) across the three models in FP16.
   - Compression sweep: AWQ and GPTQ variants at 1k prompts; FP8 only for the single candidate (rwinf-13B-opt) and only on short-form subset initially.
   - Metrics: ROUGE-L / BERTScore against gold summaries, human-rated clinical fidelity on 200 cases, token latency distribution, and per-token cost estimate.

4) Success criteria (proposal):
   - Triage: p50 < 200ms for 16–32 token prompts on Mistral-Instruct-7B AWQ.
   - Summarization: no more than a 5% drop in human clinical-fidelity rating vs FP16 baseline for candidate compressed models.
   - Cost: AWQ configuration yields >=2x cost reduction vs FP16 while meeting above SLAs.

Attachments: PoC scope (orion_poc_map.xlsx), eval prompt set v2 (eval_prompt_set_v2.txt). I also exported a short benchmark CSV for reference (benchmarks_720p.csv).

Next steps:
- If that plan looks good, can we lock a kickoff for next Tuesday (Sep 1) to run the baseline FP16 sweep and align on the human-rater rubric?
- Please confirm who on your side will provision the sample EHR subset for the human-rated cases (PII-safe subset).

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min follow-up to walk through the PoC map.

Best,
Ben Carter

1) FP8 concerns: for long clinical summaries (≥3 paragraphs) how frequently have you observed hallucination or omission regressions when moving to FP8? We can't accept systematic deletions of medication mentions.
2) For AWQ vs GPTQ — which do you recommend as the first compression pass? On prior projects we've seen GPTQ give better size but sometimes obvious formatting glitches.
3) Can you share the benchmark CSV you mentioned (token-level latency + cost) and a short example of the human-rated rubric?

We can provision a redacted EHR subset for the 200 human-rated cases — I'll confirm with legal. Also Tuesday Sep 1 at 10am PT should work on our side for a kickoff if you can do that.

Hi Asha — good questions, short answers and links below.

On FP8 risk: in our internal AWQ/FP8 trade studies across clinical-style long-form prompts we observed:
- FP8 shows occasional token-level degradation on long, enumerated sections (meds, allergies) — ~3–6% of cases where a token drop or mis-ordering occurs compared to FP16.
- AWQ (8-bit asymmetric) had a much smaller delta (~1–2% of cases) and was easier to roll back for any failing prompt.

Recommendation: run AWQ first as the compression pass for the PoC baseline; reserve FP8 for a targeted short-form path only after human validation. GPTQ is acceptable as a second pass if you need extra compression but treat it as higher inspection risk for summaries.

Benchmarks & rubric: attached benchmark CSV (benchmarks_720p.csv) with per-model latency/cost estimates. Human rubric excerpt: 1) factual completeness (0–3), 2) medication mention accuracy (0–3), 3) hallucination presence (binary), 4) overall usefulness (0–3). We suggest 200 human-rated cases sampled across note lengths (short/medium/long).

Next actions:
- I'll run the FP16 baseline sweep for Llama-3-13B and rwinf-13B-opt tomorrow morning and share raw results by EOD.
- Jasmine will coordinate the AWQ sweep and initial latency runs (Jasmine: can you target the AWQ runs for Wed morning?).
- Marissa: can you prepare a short A/B evaluation template for the human raters?

Confirming kickoff: Tue Sep 1, 10:00am PT — sending calendar invite after this thread.

Thanks — I attached eval_prompt_set_v2.txt (small refresh) and included a link to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_eval_prompts

Best,
Ben
